segments.summary: A quarantine warning arrives too late; officials relay urgent messages across the system trying to reroute the ship, culminating in passing the problem to Channing.

gacd.goal: Reroute the Empress of Kolain before it reaches quarantined Venus
gacd.action: Officials relay urgent warnings and messages across space attempting to hold/contact the ship
gacd.conflict: Ship left thirty seconds before the warning; cannot be reached directly

segments.reason: Sequence has a clear goal (reroute the ship), on-stage action (frantic messaging) meeting resistance (ship already gone/unreachable); interim result passes problem to Channing.

segments.summary: In his office, Channing, Arden, and Franks debate the seemingly impossible task of contacting a ship in flight and resolve to tackle it.

gacd.goal: Find a way to contact the invisible, unreachable Empress of Kolain
gacd.action: The trio brainstorm and argue over the physics of beaming a spaceship
gacd.conflict: Every proposed method (beam, broadcast, chase ship) is shown to be impossible

segments.reason: Unified time/place (office). Goal to contact ship, action of problem-solving meeting strong conflict (impossibility), interim outcome is a commitment to try. Dominant function is problem-attack, so dramatic_scene.

segments.summary: In the diner, Charles Thomas debunks the mass-detector idea; Channing then works out the tablecloth math for beaming via Mars, and they order the cam built.

cohesion.place: Dining room/bar then machine shop, Venus Equilateral

gacd.goal: Devise a workable method to aim a beam at the ship
gacd.action: Debate methods, reject mass detectors, then derive the angular-position math and design the cam
gacd.conflict: Thomas demolishes proposals; the astronomy/physics resists a solution

segments.reason: Continuous problem-solving with strong conflict (methods shot down) resolving to a working plan and ordered hardware. Diner-to-machine-shop is continuous action with no major time jump.

segments.summary: First beam attempt: they fire the cam-controlled beam and get no reflection; Franks realizes the reflected wave returns off-angle and they resolve to build a range finder.

gacd.goal: Contact the ship by beaming and detecting a reflection
gacd.action: Fire and waggle the beam, waiting for a return signal
gacd.conflict: Receiver stays silent; hours of failure

segments.reason: On-stage attempt with strong conflict (repeated failure) leading to interim insight (off-angle reflection). Same time/place (beam control room).

cohesion.place: Central channel / ends of Venus Equilateral

segments.reason: Largely logistical construction and alignment banter over hours; no strong on-stage conflict/outcome and no decisive ERAC deliberation. Unified by the mirror-mounting task.

segments.start_exact: Once again the signal lashed out.
segments.summary: Renewed beam attempts fail until Channing devises an electronic scanning 'shotgun' sweep; the dancing beam finally gets a return signal from the ship.

gacd.goal: Get a detectable reflection confirming the ship's position
gacd.action: Fire the beam, fail, then implement an electronically dancing scanning beam
gacd.conflict: Continued silence/failure with the fixed beam

segments.reason: Goal, on-stage action (new scanning method) against ongoing failure, resolved with the return signal ('Got 'em'). Continuous time/place.

segments.summary: Franks devises keying the beam in Morse on the ship's meteor-spotter frequency; they secure a toy key, build a thyratron keyer, retune the transmitter, and begin sending.

cohesion.place: Beam Control Room / lab, Venus Equilateral

gacd.goal: Send an intelligible message via the beam to the ship
gacd.action: Design and build the keying scheme, retune the transmitter, and begin transmitting code
gacd.conflict: Technical problems: intermittent contact, keying a huge load, retuning frequency

segments.reason: Continuous engineering scene with a goal to transmit a message, on-stage building against technical obstacles, ending with the message being sent. Same location.

The _Empress of Kolain_ was zipping along in its silent passage
through the void.
segments.summary: Aboard the Empress of Kolain, life proceeds uneventfully; passengers dine, swim, and play as the ship follows its erratic but confident course.
segments.reason: Scene shifts to the ship; descriptive establishment of shipboard normalcy with no goal/conflict. Unified by place (the liner).

segments.summary: Officer Hendall deduces the false 'meteor' is a signal, finds young Freddy Thomas who reads the Morse message, and orders the course change to Terra.

gacd.action: Hendall investigates, deduces it's a coded transmission, summons a code-reader, and decodes the message

segments.reason: On-stage detective work with obstacles (undecipherable signal, no code-knower) resolved by decoding and the course-change order. Unified on the bridge.

segments.summary: Confirming the ship answered, Channing shuts down, reflects on the achievement, and plans to turn spaceship-contacting into a routine service.

erac.reason: The ship answered; the job is essentially done
erac.anticipation: They'll be chasing spaceships all the way to Pluto and perfecting the technique
erac.choice: Shut down, clean up, refine it into a service, and owe the gang a dinner

segments.reason: Post-success wind-down: reaction plus reasoning about the future and a decision to develop the technique. No on-stage conflict; fits ERAC.
